nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functions $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ with $x < f(x)$ for every $f \in F$ and every $x \in \mathbb{N}$, let $s \in \mathbb{N}$, and let $C \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ be a fixed-point set for $F$ and $s$: $y \in C$ exactly when $y = s$ or $y = f(x)$ for some $f \in F$ and $x \in C$. Then $C$ equals the set generated from $s$ by $F$, the numbers obtained from $s$ by applying finitely many…
nodes.title: Under strict growth, a fixed-point set is the generated set

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functions $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ with $x < f(x)$ for every $f \in F$ and every $x \in \mathbb{N}$, and let $s \in \mathbb{N}$. If $C$ is a fixed-point set for $F$ and $s$, then $C$ is the intersection of all sets $G \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ that contain $s$ and are closed under every $f \in F$.
nodes.title: Under strict growth, a fixed-point set is the intersection of all self-generating sets

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functions $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ with $x < f(x)$ for every $f \in F$ and every $x \in \mathbb{N}$, and let $s \in \mathbb{N}$. If $C$ is a fixed-point set for $F$ and $s$, then $C$ contains $s$ and is closed under every $f \in F$, and $C \subseteq G$ for every set $G \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ that contains $s$ and is closed under every $f \in F$.
nodes.title: Under strict growth, a fixed-point set is the least self-generating set

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functions $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and $s \in \mathbb{N}$. Every fixed-point set $C$ for $F$ and $s$ is self-generating: $s \in C$, and $f(x) \in C$ for every $f \in F$ and every $x \in C$.
nodes.title: Fixed-point sets are self-generating

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functions $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ with $x < f(x)$ for every $f \in F$ and every $x \in \mathbb{N}$, and let $s \in \mathbb{N}$. If $C_1$ and $C_2$ are both fixed-point sets for $F$ and $s$, then $C_1 = C_2$.
nodes.title: Under strict growth, fixed-point sets are unique

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functions $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and let $s \in \mathbb{N}$. A set $C \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ is a fixed-point set for $F$ and $s$ when, for every $y \in \mathbb{N}$, $y \in C$ if and only if $y = s$ or $y = f(x)$ for some $f \in F$ and some $x \in C$; equivalently, $C = \{s\} \cup \bigcup_{f \in F} f(C)$.
nodes.title: Fixed-point sets for a seed and generators

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functions $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and let $s \in \mathbb{N}$. Reachability from $s$ is the least predicate on $\mathbb{N}$ that holds at $s$ and holds at $f(w)$ whenever it holds at $w$ and $f \in F$. Thus $y$ is reachable exactly when $y = f_k(\cdots f_1(s) \cdots)$ for some $k \ge 0$ and $f_1, \ldots, f_k \in F$; the case $k = 0$ is $s$ itself.
nodes.title: Reachability from a seed by generators

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functions $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and $s \in \mathbb{N}$. The set generated from $s$ by $F$ equals the intersection of all sets $G \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ that contain $s$ and are closed under every $f \in F$.
nodes.title: The generated set is the intersection of all self-generating sets

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functions $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and $s \in \mathbb{N}$, and let $\Gamma$ be the set generated from $s$ by $F$. Then for every $y \in \mathbb{N}$, $y \in \Gamma$ if and only if $y = s$ or $y = f(x)$ for some $f \in F$ and $x \in \Gamma$.
nodes.title: The generated set is a fixed-point set

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functions $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and $s \in \mathbb{N}$. The set generated from $s$ by $F$ contains $s$ and is closed under every $f \in F$: if $x$ is in it and $f \in F$, then $f(x)$ is in it.
nodes.title: The generated set is self-generating

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functions $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and let $s \in \mathbb{N}$. If a set $G \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ contains $s$ and satisfies $f(x) \in G$ for every $f \in F$ and every $x \in G$, then $G$ contains the set generated from $s$ by $F$, that is, every number obtained from $s$ by applying finitely many (possibly no) functions of $F$ in succession.
nodes.title: The generated set lies in every self-generating set

nodes.summary: For a finite set $F$ of functions $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and a seed $s \in \mathbb{N}$, the set generated from $s$ by $F$ consists of all numbers $f_k(\cdots f_1(s) \cdots)$ with $k \ge 0$ and $f_1, \dots, f_k \in F$; the case $k = 0$ gives $s$ itself.
nodes.title: Set generated from a seed

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functions $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and let $s \in \mathbb{N}$. Call a set $G \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ self-generating if $s \in G$ and $f(x) \in G$ for every $f \in F$ and every $x \in G$. If $C$ is self-generating and is contained in every self-generating set, then $C$ equals the set generated from $s$ by $F$.
nodes.title: The least self-generating set is the generated set

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functions $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and let $s \in \mathbb{N}$. A set $\Gamma \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ is self-generating for $s$ and $F$ when $s \in \Gamma$ and $f(x) \in \Gamma$ for every $f \in F$ and every $x \in \Gamma$.
nodes.title: Self-generating sets

nodes.summary: A finite set $F$ of functions $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ has strict growth when $x < f(x)$ for every $f \in F$ and every $x \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: Strict growth of a set of generators

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
